dishwasher-dimensions.title: Dishwasher Dimensions — and Why the Built-In Model Is 3 cm Shorter Than Usual
dishwasher-dimensions.description: Width, height, and depth of dishwashers by model, taken from the specification sheets in the catalog. The difference between a standard dishwasher and a built-in model isn’t just the front panel—it’s 3 cm in height and 5 cm in depth.

sections.heading: The short answer: 60 cm wide, and the height depends on the type
paragraphs: All 24 dishwashers listed in our catalog are between 59.5 and 60 cm wide. This is the standard cabinet opening size for kitchen cabinets, and it does not vary between models or brands.

What does vary is the height, which depends on the type of installation. A standard dishwasher—one with a visible front—measures between 84.5 and 85 cm in our store. A fully integrated dishwasher measures between 81.5 and 81.8 cm. The difference is entirely consistent and not coincidental.

sections.heading: Why is the integral lower?
paragraphs: A built-in dishwasher is designed to be concealed behind a kitchen cabinet door, with the cabinet door forming part of its front panel. The manufacturer lowers the height of the unit so that the appliance and the line of cabinets above it are flush with the countertop, rather than protruding above it.

The depth follows the same logic. Our built-in dishwashers measure 55 to 56 cm in depth, compared to 58.8 to 63 cm for standard models—again, to make room for a door to be added at the front while still aligning with the cabinetry.
The practical conclusion: These are two different size categories, not design variations. You cannot substitute one for the other within the same niche without checking both sizes.

sections.heading: What to Measure at Home Before Ordering
paragraphs: Cabinet opening width—requires 60 cm of clear space. Clear height from the floor to the bottom of the countertop: For a standard dishwasher, at least 86 cm is required; for a built-in model, 82–83 cm is sufficient. The depth from the front edge of the cabinets to the wall, plus 5 cm for plumbing and electrical wiring.

One detail people tend to overlook: the space needed for the door to open. A dishwasher door opens downward and extends about 55 cm forward. In a narrow kitchen, this means you can’t stand in front of the open dishwasher—and you should make sure there isn’t a kitchen island or cabinet blocking the way.

sections.heading: Narrow Dishwasher: What's Actually Available
paragraphs: There are also 45 cm-wide dishwashers on the market, designed for small kitchens or couples. Our current catalog does not include such a model—all models in stock are 60 cm wide. If you’re planning a kitchen around a narrow dishwasher, we recommend checking availability with us before finalizing your cabinetry.

faq.question: How tall is a built-in dishwasher?
faq.answer: 81.5 to 81.8 cm for the models measured in our catalog—about 3 cm shorter than a standard dishwasher, which measures between 84.5 and 85 cm. This difference is intended to make room for the kitchen door that is added to the front.

faq.question: Are all dishwashers 60 cm wide?
faq.answer: All 24 models listed in our catalog are 59.5–60 cm wide. There are also 45-cm-wide models available on the market, but our current catalog does not include any such models.

faq.question: How deep is a dishwasher?
faq.answer: Standard dishwasher: 58.8 to 63 cm. Built-in dishwasher: 55 to 56 cm. For both types, allow about 5 cm at the back for plumbing and electrical connections.

faq.question: How much space is needed to open the dishwasher door?
faq.answer: About 55 cm forward from the front edge. In a narrow kitchen or in front of a kitchen island, make sure the door opens fully and that there is enough space to stand and load items.

oven-dimensions.title: Standard Built-In Oven Dimensions — And Why Depth Is the Measurement That Can Make or Break an Order
oven-dimensions.description: Built-in oven dimensions: The width and height are nearly identical across all manufacturers, but the depth varies by up to 10 cm. A table of dimensions and niche sizes by model, and how to measure correctly.

sections.heading: The width and height are almost constant
paragraphs: A standard-size built-in oven is roughly square: Among the 32 built-in ovens measured in our catalog, the width ranges from 56 to 59.7 cm with a median of 59.5, and the height ranges from 45.5 to 60 cm with the same median of 59.5. In other words, when it comes to a “60-centimeter oven,” the product itself is almost always 59.5 by 59.5 centimeters—manufacturers leave a half-centimeter gap so it will fit into a 60-centimeter niche.

An exception is a compact oven that is 45 cm tall, designed for a shallower niche and typically used as a second oven or as an oven with a microwave function. It does not replace a standard oven in a 60-centimeter niche without custom cabinetry modifications.

sections.heading: The Depth — This Is Where the Problems Begin
paragraphs: While the width and height remain virtually unchanged, the depth of the built-in ovens measured ranges from 49.4 to 59.5 cm. This is a range of 10.1 cm between models that look identical from the outside and are sold under the same label of “60-cm built-in oven.”

The practical implication: If your cabinet is 55 cm deep, some models will fit perfectly, and others simply won’t. In addition to the cabinet’s depth, you’ll need space at the back—for the electrical outlet, for plumbing if applicable, and for the ventilation clearance required by the manufacturer. Anyone who orders based on the assumption that “they’re all 60 cm” will find this out on installation day.

sections.heading: Product Dimensions vs. Niche Dimensions
paragraphs: As with cooktops, there are two dimensions here as well. The product dimension refers to the unit itself; the niche dimension refers to the opening in the cabinet into which it fits. For the built-in ovens in our catalog, the published niche dimensions range from 56 to 56.8 cm in width and from 54.9 to 57 cm in depth, and are sometimes listed as a range with a tolerance — for example, 56–56.8 cm — because the cabinet is not measured with millimeter precision.

When a manufacturer specifies a range, measurements are based on the wider end of that range. A niche that is slightly too large will be covered by the oven panel; a niche that is too small will require additional carpentry work.

sections.heading: How to Assess an Existing Niche
paragraphs: Measure three dimensions inside the opening, not outside it: the width between the inner sides of the cabinet, the height of the opening, and the depth from the front to the back wall. Measure at three different points along each axis—old cabinets aren’t perfectly square—and use the smallest measurement.

Be sure to check the location of the electrical outlet: A built-in oven requires a dedicated outlet, and not every older kitchen comes with one already installed in the right spot. If you’re replacing an old oven, it’s a good idea to take a photo of the niche and the electrical outlet and send it to us—we’ll check for compatibility with the exact model before you place your order.

faq.question: What are the dimensions of a standard built-in oven?
faq.answer: Approximately 59.5 cm wide and 59.5 cm high for most models, for a 60 cm niche—these are the median measurements for the 32 built-in ovens listed in the catalog. Depth is the variable measurement: it ranges from 49.4 to 59.5 cm.

faq.question: Are all ovens built to the same depth?
faq.answer: No, and that’s the most common mistake. The width and height are almost identical across manufacturers, but the depth varies by up to 10.1 cm. Measure the depth of the cabinet before choosing a model.

faq.question: How high should a niche be for a compact oven?
faq.answer: A compact oven is approximately 45 cm high instead of 60 cm and requires a niche of the corresponding height. It cannot replace a standard oven in an existing 60-cm niche without modifying the cabinetry.

faq.question: I have a non-standard-sized niche—what should I do?
faq.answer: This is common in older kitchens. Send us the exact measurements of the opening; in some cases, a model will fit as-is, and in others, a minor carpentry adjustment will close the gap. We’ll check before you buy, not after.

cooktop-dimensions.title: Standard cooktop dimensions and countertop cutout sizes—the exact measurements
cooktop-dimensions.description: Cooktop widths: 30, 60, 75, and 80 cm—and the countertop cutout size required for each. A table showing measurements by model, and the difference between the product dimensions and the cutout dimensions.

sections.heading: Two different sizes, and only one of them matters to the carpenter
paragraphs: Every built-in cooktop has two dimensions that must not be confused. The product dimensions are the width and depth of the outer surface—what you see on the countertop. The cutout size (or “recess”) is the hole that needs to be cut in the countertop, and it is always smaller, because the unit sits on top of it and covers the edges.

The difference between the two is not fixed. For the 19 models in the catalog that list both the product size and the cut size, the difference in width ranges from 2 to 4.5 cm. This is precisely why you cannot derive the cut size from the product width—you need the number published by the manufacturer, which is the number listed in the table below.

sections.heading: The actual dimensions
paragraphs: Among the cooktops listed in our catalog, the widths fall into three distinct groups: narrow “Domino” models ranging from 28.8 to 30 cm, the most common standard size of 55.5 to 60 cm—which includes most models—and wide cooktops ranging from 64.6 to 80 cm. The depth remains virtually unchanged: all built-in cooktops range from 51 to 52.4 cm, with the sole exception being a portable double cooktop that is 32 cm deep. The thickness (height) ranges from 4.5 to 13 cm, with the difference primarily due to the legs.

The cutout dimensions correspond to these groups. In the standard width group, all models that specify a cutout dimension require a width of 56 cm, and two of them specify a range of up to 56.2 cm. For the Domino models, the cutout dimensions are 26.2–26.8 cm. For wide cooktops, only one cutout size was listed in the catalog: 75–75.2 cm, for the 80-cm model. For six wide models, ranging from 64.6 to 75 cm, the specification sheet lists a cutout of 56 cm—the same as for the 60-cm cooktops. Such a discrepancy between the countertop and the cutout is significant enough that we would not present it without verification; therefore, these models appear in the table without a cutout measurement; Before cutting into the countertop, verify the measurement with the manufacturer. The cutout depth falls within a narrow range of 48 to 50 cm for all models.

sections.heading: Replacing an existing cooktop? Measure the cutout, not the cooktop itself.
paragraphs: When replacing a cooktop in an existing countertop, the determining factor is the existing cutout. Measure it directly on the countertop—width and depth—and look for a model whose cutout dimensions are the same as or slightly smaller than those of the existing cutout. A hole that is too small can be enlarged; a hole that is too large is almost impossible to fix without replacing the countertop.

It’s also worth measuring the distance from the edge of the cutout to the front and back edges of the countertop, as well as the distance from the wall. Manufacturers specify minimum installation clearances, which vary between gas and induction models—induction models also require ventilation and clearance from the oven below.

sections.heading: What else to check before deciding on a model
paragraphs: For gas cooktops—the location of the existing gas outlet compared to the connection point on the new model, and the number of burners and their power ratings. For induction cooktops — type of electrical connection: Some models require a dedicated circuit, and not every home electrical panel is pre-wired for this, which may require the services of an electrician.

And above all: the cabinet or the oven below. Induction cooktops require a ventilation gap from the built-in oven below them, and not every combination of oven and cooktop models meets this requirement. If you’re ordering an oven and a cooktop together, it’s worth verifying their compatibility in advance.

faq.question: What are the cutout dimensions for a 60 cm cooktop?
faq.answer: For all standard-width models for which a cutout dimension is listed, the width is 56 cm (with a range of up to 56.2 cm for two of them) and 48–50 cm in depth, but the exact measurement varies by model and is listed in the specifications sheet. It is never cut from the product’s width.

faq.question: What is the difference between the cooktop dimensions and the cutout dimensions?
faq.answer: The cooktop dimensions refer to the surface visible on the countertop; the cutout dimensions refer to the hole beneath it. The cutout is always smaller—for models that list both dimensions, the difference in width is 2 to 4.5 cm, depending on how far the cooktop extends beyond the cutout.

faq.question: What is the standard width of a cooktop?
faq.answer: The 55.5–60 cm range is the most common, and within that range, 60 cm is the standard size. Alongside these are narrow models measuring about 29–30 cm for small kitchens or as a complement, and wide cooktops ranging from 64.6 to 80 cm for large kitchens. The depth is almost identical across all models—around 51–52 cm.

faq.question: I'm replacing my cooktop—how will I know if a particular model will fit the existing cutout?
faq.answer: Measure the hole in the countertop itself and compare it to the cutout size of the model. The model is a good fit if its cutout size is equal to or smaller than the hole. Send us the hole measurements via WhatsApp, and we’ll verify compatibility with the model before you place your order.

washing-machine-dimensions.title: Washing machine dimensions — and why the depth is what brings down regulations
washing-machine-dimensions.description: Width, height and depth of washing machines by model, from the specification sheets in the catalog. The width is almost always 60 cm - what really changes is the depth, and it is this that determines whether the machine enters.

sections.heading: The short answer: 60 x 85 cm - and the depth is the story
paragraphs: A washing machine with a front opening is almost always the same two dimensions: in the 40 models measured in our catalog, the width varies between 59.5 and 60 cm and the height between 84 and 85 cm. This is no coincidence - these dimensions are derived from the width of a standard kitchen cabinet and the height of a work surface, and all manufacturers align to them.

The depth, on the other hand, ranges from 42 to 65.9 cm. That's a difference of almost 24 cm between the shallowest and deepest model - ten times the difference in width. Those who measure only the width of the niche and assume that the rest will work out, measure the only measure that does not change.

sections.heading: A machine with an upper opening is 40 cm, not 60
paragraphs: In the catalog there are eight models with an upper opening, and all of them are 40 cm wide - two thirds of the width of a machine with a front opening. In exchange, they are taller, 87.5 to 91 cm, and relatively deep: 60 to 61 cm.

This makes them a real solution for a narrow service balcony or a corner where there is no free 60 cm. Pay attention to the height: 91 cm will not fit under a standard work surface, and with an upper opening you need an opening space above the machine and not in front of it anyway.

sections.heading: Capacity changes depth, not width
paragraphs: This is the understanding that saves most mistakes. Going from 7 kg to 9 kg does not expand the machine - the drum increases in depth. In the models measured by us, 7 kg machines range in depth between 42 and 55 cm, 9 kg machines between 55 and 64 cm, and 11 to 13 kg models reach 60 to 65.9 cm.

The practical meaning: if your niche is 58 cm deep, the question is not whether a machine will fit, but what capacity it will fit. And if you are debating between 8 and 9 kg, the difference in depth may be the deciding factor, not the price.

sections.heading: What to measure at home before ordering
paragraphs: The width of the niche - and add at least 2 cm beyond the 60, so that it can be inserted and removed without scratching. Free height to the surface: a machine with a height of 85 cm needs a niche of 86-87 cm, because the legs are adjustable and the surface is not always straight. And the depth - and here you have to measure up to the wall, then add 5 to 10 cm for the plumbing and the electrical connection at the back. It's the spacing that people forget, and it's the one that makes the machine stand out from the cabinet.

Two more surprising measurements: the width of the door at the entrance to the house and at the entrance to the room. A 60 cm wide machine in the package is usually 63-65 cm, and a narrow service door could be the real problem. And if the machine goes up stairs - you should also measure the width of the stairwell at the turn.

sections.heading: Under the surface, and when it doesn't work
paragraphs: A machine with a height of 84-85 cm fits under a standard kitchen surface with a height of 90 cm, but only if there is no drawer or shelf that steals height. It is worth checking the actual available height and not the height of the surface.
If the plan is to place a dryer above the machine, the depth of the two devices should be similar, and a dedicated connection kit is needed - more on this in the dryer dimensions guide.

faq.question: What are the standard dimensions of a washing machine?
faq.answer: Machine with front opening: 59.5-60 cm wide and 84-85 cm high, according to the 40 models measured in our catalog. The depth is what changes - between 42 and 65.9 cm, depending on the capacity and model.

faq.question: How deep is a 9 kg washing machine?
faq.answer: In the 9 kg models measured by us, the depth ranges from 55 to 64 cm. For comparison, 7 kg models range from 42 to 55 cm. The width in both capacities is the same - 59.8 to 60 cm.

faq.question: Is there a washing machine narrower than 60 cm?
faq.answer: Yes — machines in the upper entrance. In our catalog there are eight such models and all of them are 40 cm wide. They are taller (87.5-91 cm) and require an opening space above the machine, not in front of it.

faq.question: How much space should be left behind the washing machine?
faq.answer: 5 to 10 cm beyond the depth of the model, the water pipe, the drain pipe and the electrical connection. This is the gap that most people forget to measure, and is the common reason why a machine stands out from the line of cabinets.

faq.question: Where do the measurements in the table come from?
faq.answer: From the manufacturer's or importer's specification sheet, as it appears in the product record in the store's catalog. A model for which an exact size has not been published does not appear in the table. Before carpentry or a final order it is always advisable to verify against the specific model.

tv-65-inch-dimensions.title: 65 inch TV dimensions - width, height and depth according to model
tv-65-inch-dimensions.description: How wide is a 65 inch TV really? A table of measured dimensions by model - with and without a stand, including the VESA standard - and what should be measured before hanging or buying a sideboard.

sections.heading: The short answer: about 144 to 146 cm wide
paragraphs: A 65-inch screen is a screen whose diagonal is 165 cm. With a 16:9 image ratio, this means that the panel itself is 143.9 cm wide and 80.9 cm high - a simple geometric calculation that does not depend on the manufacturer. The frame adds a little more: in the 65-inch models measured in our catalog, the total width varies between 144.1 and 145.6 cm and the height between 82.6 and 84.1 cm.

That is: every 65-inch TV, of any brand, occupies approximately the same width. The difference between the narrowest and widest model in the catalog is 1.5 cm. A closed niche with a width of 150 cm will accommodate any of the models; For placing on an open sideboard, a more generous space is useful, as explained below. If you are debating between 65 and 75 inches, the difference in panel width is 22 cm.

sections.heading: The depth is not what you think
paragraphs: The figure that surprises most people: the screen itself is thin - 4 to 8.4 cm in the models we measured. But as soon as the stand is assembled, the depth jumps to 22.2 to 34.5 cm. If you place on a sideboard, the depth that needs to be checked is that of the stand, not the screen. A sideboard with a depth of 30 cm can fit one model and not the other.

The height also varies: in the models for which both sizes are published, the stand raises the TV by 4 to 6.6 cm, so that the total height with the stand is 87 to 90.6 cm. This is important if there is a shelf or cabinet above.

sections.heading: Do not buy a suspension arm before choosing a model
paragraphs: This is the most expensive mistake in this category. The VESA mounting standard is not uniform between 65 inch models - in our catalog alone there are five different standards for the same screen size: 200x200, 300x200, 300x300, 400x300 and 400x400 mm. A pre-purchased "65 inch" arm may simply not screw on.

In practice, most modern arms support some standards, but not all, and the weight is a separate parameter. The correct order of operations: choose a model, check its VESA standard in the table above or in the specification sheet, and only then buy an arm.

sections.heading: What to measure at home before ordering
paragraphs: The width of the available wall or sideboard. 147-148 cm is enough for a closed niche; For an open placement, 155 cm or more is recommended, so that the screen does not look cramped and remains spacious for ventilation and cables. The depth of the sideboard, versus the depth of the stand of the particular model. The height from the floor to the shelf or cabinet above, versus the total height with a stand. And if hanging on the wall - the location of the socket and the communication point, which should be behind the screen and not next to it.
A simple tip: stick adhesive paper measuring 145 x 84 cm on the wall. It gives a more accurate feeling than any number, especially when deciding between sizes.

sections.heading: Viewing distance — and why there is no single answer
paragraphs: 4K content, which is almost everything that is broadcast today to a screen of this size, does not have a technical threshold that requires a certain distance; At this resolution, the eye does not separate pixels from a relatively short distance. In many salons in Israel, the sitting distance is 2.5-3.5 meters, and in this range 65 inches is considered a comfortable size for most people.

Personal preference has more weight than any formula. Those who like a cinema feel will prefer to sit closer or go up a size; Those who are sensitive to fast movement or mainly watch the news will prefer otherwise. If possible - you should see the size in the store from a distance similar to your living room.

faq.question: What is the exact width of a 65 inch TV?
faq.answer: The panel itself is 143.9 cm wide (65 inch diagonal in 16:9 ratio). With the frame, the 65-inch models measured in our catalog range from 144.1 to 145.6 cm. To plan a sideboard or a niche, you should lay down 146 cm and add a margin.

faq.question: What is the height of a 65 inch TV with a stand?
faq.answer: In the measured models, the height without a stand is 82.6-84.1 cm and with a stand 87-90.6 cm. The stand adds 4 to 6.6 cm. If there is a shelf above, this is the figure that needs to be checked.

faq.question: Do all 65 inch TVs fit the same hanging arm?
faq.answer: not. In our catalog there are five different 65-inch VESA standards: 200x200, 300x200, 300x300, 400x300 and 400x400 mm. Check the standard of the exact model before buying an arm.

faq.question: What is the difference in width between 65 and 75 inches?
faq.answer: About 22 cm. A 75-inch panel is 166 cm wide compared to 143.9 cm in a 65-inch panel, and in actual measurement, the 75-inch models in the catalog range from 166.6 to 167.8 cm. The difference in height between the panels is 12.5 cm, and between the measured bodies 11.7 to 14 cm.

faq.question: Where do the measurements in the table come from?
faq.answer: From the manufacturer's or importer's specification sheet, as it appears in the product record in the store's catalog. A model for which an exact size has not been published does not appear in the table. Before hanging or ordering carpentry, you should always verify against the final model.

dryer-dimensions.title: Tumble Dryer Dimensions — and Can It Be Placed on Top of the Washer?
dryer-dimensions.description: Width, height, and depth of tumble dryers by model, taken from the specification sheets in the catalog. They all have the same front panel dimensions of 60 × 85, but the depth varies by 10 cm—and the difference depends on the model, not the technology.

sections.heading: The short answer: The front panel is the same as that of a washing machine.
paragraphs: The 16 tumble dryers listed in our catalog range from 59.5 to 60 cm in width and from 84 to 85 cm in height—exactly the same front width as a front-loading washing machine. This is intentional: the dryer is designed to stand next to or on top of the washing machine.
The depth ranges from 54.6 to 65 cm. This is where, just like with the washing machine, all the variations lie—which is why this is the measurement you need to check against the niche.

sections.heading: Heat Pump or Condenser — Depth Isn’t the Deciding Factor Between Them
paragraphs: It is commonly believed that heat pump dryers are deeper because they contain a complete refrigeration cycle—a compressor, evaporator, and condenser. In the models we tested, the picture is more complex: Heat pump dryers range in depth from 54.6 to 65 cm, and condenser dryers from 57.5 to 63 cm, with the median being nearly identical—61.4 versus 61 cm. The deepest models in the catalog are indeed heat pump dryers (64–65 cm), but the shallowest one is also a heat pump dryer, at 54.6 cm. A vented dryer measured 55.5 cm.

The practical implication: A shallow niche is no reason to forgo a heat pump, which is the most energy-efficient of the technologies. If your niche is 58 cm deep, there are models of both types that will fit—choose based on the dimensions of the specific model, not the type of drying system.

sections.heading: Placing the dryer on top of the washing machine—three conditions
paragraphs: First, you need a dedicated stacking kit. Never place a tumble dryer directly on top of a washing machine: the washing machine vibrates during the spin cycle, and the tumble dryer may shift or fall. The stacking kit is designed for a width of 60 cm and connects the two appliances.

Second, the depth of both appliances should be similar. A 65-centimeter-deep dryer placed in front of a 47-centimeter-deep washing machine will protrude forward in an unstable manner. It’s a good idea to check both measurements together before placing your order.

Third, the total height. Two appliances, each 85 cm tall, measure 170 cm before the connection kit is installed, and usually a little more with the kit. This means that the door of the top dryer is at eye level or higher—convenient for most people, but it’s worth making sure you can reach it comfortably.

sections.heading: What to Measure at Home
paragraphs: A minimum clearance width of 62 cm, a minimum clearance height of 87 cm for a single dryer, and a depth of 5 cm beyond the wall for connections. If the dryer is a condenser or heat pump model, it does not require an external vent, but it does require space to empty the water tank or a drain connection.

And if the dryer is intended for a closed utility balcony—keep in mind that a condenser dryer emits heat and moisture into the room. In a small, enclosed balcony, this is noticeable, and a heat pump performs better under these conditions.

faq.question: What are the dimensions of a tumble dryer?
faq.answer: The 16 models measured in our catalog are 59.5–60 cm wide and 84–85 cm tall—the same front width as a front-loading washing machine. The depth ranges from 54.6 to 65 cm.

faq.question: Is a heat pump dryer deeper than a condenser dryer?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. In the models we tested, the heat pump ranged from 54.6 to 65 cm and the condenser from 57.5 to 63 cm, with an almost identical median. The deepest ones are heat pumps, but so are the shallowest—which is why you should check the specific model itself.

faq.question: Can you place a tumble dryer on top of a washing machine?
faq.answer: Yes, but only with a special connection kit—not directly. Also, the depth of both appliances should be similar; otherwise, the dryer will stick out. The total height will be about 170 cm or more.

faq.question: Does a tumble dryer need an exhaust hose?
faq.answer: Condenser and heat pump dryers do not require an exhaust vent to the outside—they collect moisture in a tank or drain it away. A dryer with an exhaust vent does require an opening to the outside. In our catalog, most models are condenser or heat pump dryers.

refrigerator-4-door-dimensions.title: Dimensions of a 4-door refrigerator—90 cm wide, and that’s the number that matters
refrigerator-4-door-dimensions.description: Width, height, and depth of 4-door refrigerators by model, taken from the specification sheets in the catalog. A 4-door refrigerator is about 30 cm wider than a 60-cm narrow refrigerator—and that’s what determines whether it will even fit.

sections.heading: The short answer: About 90 cm wide
paragraphs: Among the 20 four-door refrigerators measured in our catalog, the width ranges from 79.4 to 91.4 cm, with most models centered around 90 cm. The height ranges from 177.5 to 190 cm and the depth from 60 to 87 cm—60 to 73.1 cm in 15 of them, 77 to 78.2 cm in four models, and 87 cm in one model.

For comparison, a narrow refrigerator with a bottom freezer in our catalog is 59.5 to 60 cm wide. In other words, anyone replacing a slim refrigerator with a 4-door model is typically adding about 30 cm in width—not a design upgrade, but a change in kitchen layout.

sections.heading: Width is the constraint, not volume
paragraphs: Most people look for a refrigerator based on liters and realize too late how wide it is. In reality, it works the other way around: the niche determines the width, the width determines the type of refrigerator, and the type of refrigerator determines the range of capacities available to you.

A 70-cm niche won’t fit a 4-door refrigerator, even if the capacity is suitable for a family. A 95-centimeter niche will comfortably accommodate most models. For niches between 80 and 90 centimeters, you’ll need to check each model individually—that’s where most of the variation lies.

sections.heading: Door clearance — the measurement that isn’t listed anywhere
paragraphs: A 4-door refrigerator consists of two upper doors that open to the sides and two lower drawers. The advantage is that each upper door is relatively narrow, so it requires less space to open than the door of a wide, single-door refrigerator.

The drawback lies in the drawers. A drawer slides out to its full depth, so you need free space in front of the refrigerator that is at least as deep as the refrigerator itself—that is, 60 to 73.1 cm for most models. In a kitchen with a central island, this is the determining factor: the distance between the front of the refrigerator and the island must allow both for the drawer to be pulled out and for a person to stand there.

Another factor to consider: If the refrigerator is placed against a side wall, a door that opens toward the wall may hit it before reaching a 90-degree angle, preventing the interior drawers from pulling out fully. Most models have a preferred opening side—it’s worth asking before placing your order.

sections.heading: Height, and what’s above the refrigerator
paragraphs: The heights listed in the catalog range from 177.5 to 190 cm. The 12.5-cm difference between the shortest and tallest models falls precisely within the range where a wall cabinet above the refrigerator goes from being a problem to a solution—or vice versa.

It’s best to leave 5 to 10 cm above the refrigerator for condenser ventilation. A refrigerator that is squeezed into a closed niche that is exactly its height will work harder and consume more electricity. If there is a built-in upper cabinet, measure the available height to the bottom of the cabinet, not to the ceiling.

sections.heading: What to Measure at Home Before Ordering
paragraphs: Niche width—add 2 to 3 cm on each side for installation clearance and ventilation. The available height to the cabinet or ceiling, plus ventilation clearance. The depth to the wall, as well as the depth by which the refrigerator will protrude from the line of cabinets—a 73-cm-deep refrigerator protrudes significantly from a 60-cm-deep kitchen, which affects both the appearance and the clearance.

And finally, the delivery route: the width of the front door, the width of the hallway, and the turn in the stairwell. A 90-cm-wide refrigerator in its packaging measures about 95 cm, and in older buildings in the north, this is often the deciding factor. If in doubt—you can send us the measurements, and we’ll check them against the model before you place your order.

faq.question: How wide is a 4-door refrigerator?
faq.answer: 79.4 to 91.4 cm across the 20 models measured in our catalog, with most models around 90 cm. By comparison, a slim refrigerator with a bottom-mounted freezer is 59.5 to 60 cm wide in our catalog.

faq.question: How much space does a 4-door refrigerator require?
faq.answer: Most models require a niche of approximately 95 cm—the width of the refrigerator plus 2–3 cm on each side for installation and ventilation. A niche of 80–90 cm requires verification with the specific model.

faq.question: How much space do you need in front of a 4-door refrigerator?
faq.answer: At least the depth of the refrigerator—60 to 73.1 cm in most models—is necessary so that the lower drawers can be pulled out completely. In a kitchen with a central island, this is usually the determining factor, more so than the width of the refrigerator itself.

faq.question: How tall is a 4-door refrigerator?
faq.answer: 177.5 to 190 cm in the models we measured. It’s a good idea to leave 5 to 10 cm of space above the refrigerator for condenser ventilation—a refrigerator that’s squeezed into a closed niche that’s exactly its height consumes more electricity.

faq.question: Where do the measurements in the table come from?
faq.answer: From the manufacturer’s or importer’s specification sheet, as it appears in the product listing in the store’s catalog. Models for which no exact dimensions have been published do not appear in the table.

tv-75-inch-dimensions.title: 75-inch TV Dimensions — Width, Height, and Depth by Model
tv-75-inch-dimensions.description: A 75-inch TV is approximately 167 cm wide, and its stand is up to 39 cm deep. A table of measurements by model—with and without the stand, including VESA standards—and what to check on the wall and on the TV stand before ordering.

sections.heading: The short answer: About 167 cm wide
paragraphs: The diagonal measurement is 75 inches: 75 × 2.54 = 190.5 cm. With a 16:9 aspect ratio, the panel itself is 166 cm wide and 93.4 cm high. Among the 12 75-inch models for which the physical dimensions were published, the total width ranges from 166.6 to 167.8 cm, and the height ranges from 95.8 to 96.6 cm.

As with any size, the brand makes almost no difference in width—the difference between models is 1.2 cm. Compared to a 65-inch model, this is an increase of about 22 cm in width and 12.5 cm in height: a wall that looks spacious with a 65-inch model may look crowded with a 75-inch one.

sections.heading: The Sideboard: Here, 75 inches really is different
paragraphs: At this size, the stand is large. Among the 11 models for which the depth including the stand is listed, it ranges from 28 to 39.1 cm. A 30-cm-deep cabinet will only fit one of them; a 35-cm-deep cabinet will fit four; only a 40-cm-deep cabinet will accommodate all of them. Anyone replacing a smaller TV on the same cabinet should check this before choosing a model.

The unit itself is slim—3.1 to 10.3 cm—so when mounted on the wall, the issue of depth is virtually eliminated. The stand raises the TV by 5 to 7.7 cm, and the total height with the stand ranges from 100.8 to 104.2 cm.

The width of the stand is also important: in some models, the legs are positioned close to the edges of the TV, in which case the stand needs to be almost as wide as the entire TV. The placement of the legs is shown in the diagram included in the specifications sheet for each model.

sections.heading: VESA Standard: Four standards of the same size
paragraphs: Among the 10 75-inch models listed in the table for which mounting standards are provided, four standards appear: 300×300, 400×300, 400×400, and 500×300 mm. At this size, the weight of the TV also becomes a serious consideration, and the mount must be able to support both.
Customers should purchase a mount only after selecting a model and checking its specifications in the table or datasheet. Mounting a 167-centimeter-wide TV is a job for at least two people.

sections.heading: What to Measure at Home Before Ordering
paragraphs: Wall or cabinet width: A closed niche requires at least 170 cm. Cabinet depth corresponds to the depth of the stand for that specific model. Height to the shelf or cabinet above corresponds to the height with the stand. And if mounting on the wall—an outlet and a communication port behind the TV; the center of the TV is approximately 48 cm above its bottom edge.

And don’t forget to check the entrance: the box for a 75-inch TV is wider than the TV itself, so it’s worth checking in a narrow stairwell. A tip to get a sense of the size: Stick a piece of tape on the wall measuring 167 × 96 cm.

faq.question: How wide is a 75-inch TV?
faq.answer: The panel is 166 cm. Including the frame, the 75-inch models listed in our catalog range from 166.6 to 167.8 cm. For a built-in niche, you should plan for at least 170 cm.

faq.question: How many centimeters is 75 inches?
faq.answer: 190.5 cm diagonally (75 × 2.54). The width of a 16:9 TV of this size is 166 cm, and the height is 93.4 cm.

faq.question: What depth of TV stand is needed for a 75-inch TV?
faq.answer: The depth of the base in the models measured ranges from 28 to 39.1 cm. A 40-cm-deep sideboard fits all of them, a 35-cm-deep one fits four out of 11, and a 30-cm-deep one fits only one.

faq.question: What is the difference in size between 65 and 75 inches?
faq.answer: A 75-inch panel is 22.1 cm wider (166 vs. 143.9 cm) and 12.5 cm taller. Among the models we measured, the 65-inch model is up to 145.6 cm wide, and the 75-inch model starts at 166.6 cm.

faq.question: Where do the measurements in the table come from?
faq.answer: From the manufacturer’s or importer’s specification sheet, as it appears in the product listing in the store’s catalog. Models for which exact dimensions have not been published do not appear in the table. Before installing or ordering custom cabinetry, it is advisable to verify the dimensions against the final model.

narrow-refrigerator-60cm.title: 60 cm-wide slim-line refrigerator — dimensions, capacities, and top- or bottom-mounted freezer
narrow-refrigerator-60cm.description: Refrigerators 60 cm wide in our catalog have a capacity of up to 344 liters. Dimensions vary by model—height 141 to 187 cm, depth 57 to 70 cm—and what is the difference between a top-freezer and a bottom-freezer model of the same width?

sections.heading: The short answer: Up to 344 liters, 60 wide
paragraphs: Nine freestanding refrigerators with a width of up to 61 cm were listed in our catalog. Their width ranges from 54.9 to 60 cm, their height from 141.2 to 187 cm, their depth from 56.8 to 69.5 cm, and their capacity from 260 to 344 liters. This is the upper limit for this width: anyone who needs more than 344 liters will need a wider niche.

The next size up in the catalog is 70 cm—we don’t carry any upright refrigerators that measure between 60 and 70 cm—and there, ten out of 11 models range from 381 to 470 liters. The exception is a 329-liter model, so width alone does not guarantee a larger capacity: compare the liters of one model to another.

sections.heading: Top-freezer or bottom-freezer models of the same width
paragraphs: Five of the models have a top-mounted freezer and four have a bottom-mounted freezer. The most noticeable difference is in height: the models with a top-mounted freezer are shorter, 141.2 to 176.5 cm, while the four models with bottom-mounted freezers are taller—185 to 187 cm—with a capacity of 300 to 344 liters.

A 60-wide bottom-freezer model is convenient for those who mainly open the refrigerator compartment, since the shelves used daily are at eye level. However, if there is an upper cabinet above the niche, a unit measuring 185 cm plus ventilation clearance may not fit—in which case, a top-mounted freezer with a height of 169–176.5 cm is the solution.

sections.heading: Depth: Only two in the cabinet line
paragraphs: Of the nine models, only two are 60 cm deep or less: 56.8 and 59.2 cm. The rest are 64 to 69.5 cm deep and will protrude from kitchen cabinets, which are typically about 60 cm deep. In a narrow kitchen, where a narrow refrigerator is chosen due to lack of space, this protrusion is often more important than the width.

sections.heading: A 60-cm niche: What actually fits
paragraphs: Two of the models are exactly 60 cm wide, and six are between 59.4 and 59.5 cm wide. In a niche that is exactly 60 cm wide, they are flush against the walls, with no clearance for installation and no ventilation gap—and in most cases, this doesn’t work. The exact requirement is listed in the installation instructions for each model, and it’s a good idea to check it before placing an order.

For an exceptionally narrow niche, there are two options: The narrowest model measured, at 54.9 cm, is a 260-liter top-freezer refrigerator that is 141.2 cm tall. A built-in refrigerator is 54 cm wide, but it is designed for installation inside a cabinet and requires a dedicated niche—see the guide to built-in refrigerators.

faq.question: What capacity refrigerator fits in a 60 cm wide space?
faq.answer: Up to 344 liters in the models listed in our catalog—for both top-freezer and bottom-freezer models. The full range is 260 to 344 liters.

faq.question: Do you have a 60 cm wide bottom-freezer refrigerator?
faq.answer: Yes. Four models were measured, ranging from 59.5 to 60 cm in width and 300 to 344 liters in capacity. They are the tallest models in this width range: 185 to 187 cm.

faq.question: How deep is a slim refrigerator?
faq.answer: 56.8 to 69.5 cm in the models measured. Only two out of nine are 60 cm deep or less, so most of the narrow refrigerators protrude beyond the line of the cabinets.

faq.question: Will a 60-wide refrigerator fit into a 60-centimeter niche?
faq.answer: It’s usually not a good fit. Without space on the sides, it’s hard to install the refrigerator, and most manufacturers also require ventilation space. Check the requirements in the model’s installation instructions, or send us the niche dimensions and we’ll check for you.

faq.question: Where do the measurements in the table come from?
faq.answer: From the manufacturer’s or importer’s specification sheet, as it appears in the product listing in the store’s catalog. Models for which exact dimensions have not been published do not appear in the table. Built-in refrigerators are listed in a separate guide.

refrigerator-dimensions.title: Standard refrigerator dimensions—width, height, and depth by type
refrigerator-dimensions.description: How much space do you need for a refrigerator? The home refrigerators in our catalog come in four widths—approximately 60, 70, 80, and 90 cm—and depths ranging from 55 to 87 cm. A table of dimensions by model, and what to measure before ordering.

sections.heading: The short answer: Four widths, not a continuous range
paragraphs: Of the 73 household refrigerators measured in our catalog, the width ranges from 54 to 91.4 cm, the height from 141.2 to 203 cm, and the depth from 55 to 87 cm. But the range is misleading: The widths are not scattered across the range; they cluster into four groups.

14 models ranging from 54 to 60 cm in width (including five built-in models that are 54 cm wide), 12 models ranging from 69 to 70.5 cm in width, 26 models ranging from 75 to 84 cm in width, and 21 models ranging from 86 to 91.4 cm in width. There are no models available in the 60–69 cm or 70.5–75 cm ranges. Someone with a 66 cm niche, for example, will effectively choose from the 60 cm series.

sections.heading: The width determines the type and capacity
paragraphs: Approx. 60 cm: top- or bottom-freezer models, up to 344 liters in the models tested. Approx. 70 cm: 329 to 470 liters. Ten of the 11 freestanding models measured have a top-mounted freezer, and none of them are labeled as having a bottom-mounted freezer—a bottom-mounted freezer of this width is available only in one built-in model, which is 69 cm wide. 75 to 84 cm: top-freezer, bottom-freezer, and some 4-door refrigerators, 427 to 680 liters. 86 to 91.4 cm: Mainly 4- and 5-door refrigerators, 572 to 819 liters.

In other words, most people search by liters, but the niche determines the choice first. The niche determines the width, the width determines which models are available, and the model determines the range of capacities. Details for each width can be found in the dedicated guides: 60-width narrow refrigerators, 70-width refrigerators, 4-door refrigerators, and built-in refrigerators.

sections.heading: Depth: Most refrigerators protrude from the line of cabinets
paragraphs: The median depth in the catalog is 72 cm. 41 of the 73 models are deeper than 70 cm, and 14 are deeper than 75 cm, up to 87 cm. Compared to kitchen cabinets, which are typically about 60 cm deep, this means that most refrigerators protrude a good few centimeters forward.

It’s not just a matter of appearance. A refrigerator that protrudes 15 cm narrows the passageway in front of it, and in a kitchen with a central island or an adjacent door, that’s the difference between a comfortable kitchen and a cramped one. If depth is important to you, scan the table visually based on the “Depth” column before looking at the capacity.

sections.heading: The height, and what’s above the refrigerator
paragraphs: 29 of the 73 models are shorter than 180 cm, and 14 are taller than 185 cm; the tallest model in the catalog is 203 cm. If there is a wall cabinet above the niche, measure to the bottom of the cabinet, not to the ceiling.

It is recommended to leave 5 to 10 cm of space above the refrigerator for condenser ventilation. A refrigerator that is squeezed into a closed niche that is exactly its height will work harder and consume more electricity. The exact requirement is listed in the installation instructions for each model.

sections.heading: What to Measure at Home Before Ordering
paragraphs: The width of the niche, and leaving space for installation and ventilation according to the manufacturer’s instructions—a 60-cm-wide refrigerator will not fit comfortably into a niche that is exactly 60 cm wide. The clearance height to the cabinet. The depth to the wall, and how far the refrigerator will protrude from the line of the cabinets. And the direction in which the door opens: a door that opens toward an adjacent wall may not open to 90 degrees, in which case the interior drawers cannot be fully pulled out.

And finally, the access route: the width of the front door, the hallway, and the turn in the stairwell. If you’re unsure, send us the measurements via WhatsApp and we’ll check them against the model before you place your order.

faq.question: How wide is a standard refrigerator?
faq.answer: There is no single width. The home refrigerators in our catalog fall into four width ranges: 54–60 cm, 69–70.5 cm, 75–84 cm, and 86–91.4 cm. There are no models that measure between 60 and 69 cm or between 70.5 and 75 cm.

faq.question: How deep is a refrigerator?
faq.answer: 55 to 87 cm in the models measured, with a median of 72 cm. More than half of the models are deeper than 70 cm, and therefore protrude from kitchen cabinets, which are typically about 60 cm deep.

faq.question: How tall is a refrigerator?
faq.answer: 141.2 to 203 cm. 29 out of 73 models measured are less than 180 cm tall. Leave 5 to 10 cm of space above the refrigerator for ventilation, according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

faq.question: Which refrigerator fits into a 65-centimeter niche?
faq.answer: Only refrigerators in the 60 series: Our catalog does not include any models measuring between 60 and 69 cm in width. This category comfortably accommodates models ranging from 54.9 to 60 cm in width, with a capacity of up to 344 liters.

faq.question: Where do the measurements in the table come from?
faq.answer: From the manufacturer’s or importer’s specification sheet, as it appears in the product listing in the store’s catalog. Models for which exact dimensions have not been published do not appear in the table. Office refrigerators and display refrigerators are listed in a separate guide.

tv-55-inch-dimensions.title: Dimensions of 55-inch TVs—width, height, and depth by model
tv-55-inch-dimensions.description: How wide is a 55-inch TV? 139.7 cm diagonally, about 123 cm in actual width. A table of measurements by model—with and without the stand, including VESA standards—and what to measure before mounting or buying a TV stand.

sections.heading: The short answer: About 123 cm wide
paragraphs: 55 inches is the diagonal: 55 × 2.54 = 139.7 cm. With a 16:9 aspect ratio, the panel itself is 121.8 cm wide and 68.5 cm high—a geometric calculation that does not depend on the manufacturer. The bezel adds a little: among the seven 55-inch models for which the body dimensions were published, the width ranges from 122.5 to 123.7 cm and the height from 70.6 to 71.7 cm.

The difference between the narrow and wide models is 1.2 cm, meaning the brand makes almost no change to the width. What does make a difference, however, is the size: going from 55 to 65 inches adds 22.1 cm to the panel’s width and 12.4 cm to its height. That’s the difference between a TV that fits into a 125-centimeter niche and one that doesn’t.

sections.heading: Depth: The TV is thin, but the stand isn't
paragraphs: The unit itself is 4.6 to 7.7 cm deep in the models measured. With the stand, the depth increases to 19.9 to 29.7 cm, and for this sideboard, that’s the determining factor. A 30-cm-deep sideboard will accommodate all eight models for which a depth with the stand is listed; a 25-cm-deep sideboard will accommodate only three of them.

The stand raises the TV by 5.1 to 6.7 cm, so the total height with the stand is 75.9 to 78.4 cm. If there is a shelf above the cabinet, measure based on the height with the stand rather than the height of the TV.

sections.heading: VESA Standard: Three standards of the same size
paragraphs: Among the six 55-inch models for which mounting standards are listed, three different standards appear: 200×200, 300×200, and 300×300 mm. A mounting arm purchased in advance “for a 55-inch model” may not fit the model you choose.
The correct procedure: Choose a model, check its VESA standard in the table or spec sheet, and only then buy a mount. The TV’s weight is a separate parameter that the mount must support.

sections.heading: What to Measure at Home Before Ordering
paragraphs: Niche or cabinet width: For a closed niche, 125 cm is sufficient for all models in the table; for open placement, a more generous space is recommended for ventilation and cables. The depth of the cabinet versus the depth of the model’s stand. The height to the shelf above versus the height including the stand. And if mounting on the wall—the location of the outlet and the communication port, which should be behind the TV.

The center of the TV is about 35 cm above the bottom edge of the unit, and this measurement helps you position the outlet so that it is out of sight. Here’s a simple way to get a sense of the size: Stick a piece of tape measuring 123 × 71 cm on the wall.

sections.heading: 55 or 65?
paragraphs: This decision is usually made based on wall space rather than in the store. If the available width is 125–140 cm, 55 inches is the largest size that will fit; a 65-inch model starts at 144.1 cm in our catalog. If there is 150 cm or more, both sizes will fit, and the decision comes down to viewing distance and personal preference.

In a bedroom or small living room, where the distance from the sofa to the wall is short, a 55-inch TV is a common choice. It’s a good idea to view both sizes in the store from a distance similar to that in your home before deciding based on the number.

faq.question: How wide is a 55-inch TV?
faq.answer: The panel itself measures 121.8 cm (55 inches diagonally at a 16:9 aspect ratio). Including the frame, the 55-inch models listed in our catalog range from 122.5 to 123.7 cm. When planning a niche, it’s best to allow for 124 cm and add some extra space.

faq.question: How many centimeters is 55 inches?
faq.answer: 139.7 cm diagonally (55 × 2.54). This is not the width: the width of a 16:9 TV of this size is 121.8 cm, and the height is 68.5 cm.

faq.question: How tall is a 55-inch TV with a stand?
faq.answer: Without the stand: 70.6–71.7 cm; with the stand: 75.9–78.4 cm for models for which dimensions are listed. The stand adds 5.1 to 6.7 cm.

faq.question: What depth of TV stand do I need for a 55-inch TV?
faq.answer: The depth of the base in the models measured ranges from 19.9 to 29.7 cm. A 30-cm-deep sideboard fits all of them; a 25-cm-deep one fits only three out of eight. Check the table for the specific model.

faq.question: Where do the measurements in the table come from?
faq.answer: From the manufacturer’s or importer’s specification sheet, as it appears in the product listing in the store’s catalog. Models for which exact dimensions have not been published do not appear in the table. Before installing or ordering custom cabinetry, it is advisable to verify the dimensions against the final model.

office-refrigerator-dimensions.title: Office refrigerator sizes — a 50 cm tall mini-bar or an 85 cm tall refrigerator
office-refrigerator-dimensions.description: The office refrigerators in our catalog come in two heights: a 50-liter mini-bar, 44–51 cm tall, and an 80–99-liter refrigerator, 82.5–85 cm tall. Dimensions are measured by model, and here’s what to check before placing one under a desk or on a countertop.

sections.heading: The short answer: two heights
paragraphs: 16 office refrigerators were reviewed in our catalog, and they fall into two distinct groups. Five 50-liter mini-bar models: 44 to 48 cm wide, 44 to 51 cm tall, and 44 to 50 cm deep. And 11 models ranging from 80 to 99 liters: 43 to 52.5 cm wide, 82.5 to 85 cm tall, and 41 to 53.5 cm deep.
There’s no middle ground. Anyone looking for an office refrigerator chooses the height first—under-counter or counter-height—and only then selects a model.

sections.heading: Under the table, next to the table, or under the countertop
paragraphs: A standard office desk is usually about 72 to 75 cm high, so only the mini-bar models, which are 44 to 51 cm high, fit underneath it. The 85 models are taller than any such desk and stand next to it; their top surface is often used as a shelf for a kettle or a coffee maker.

Installing it under a kitchen countertop is more complicated. A refrigerator that’s 82.5 to 85 cm tall might fit height-wise, but office refrigerators are designed for freestanding installation and dissipate heat from the back and sides. Placing it in a closed cabinet without the clearance required by the manufacturer will cause it to work harder—so be sure to check the installation instructions before making a decision.

sections.heading: Transparent or opaque, one door or two
paragraphs: Some of the models are glass-door display refrigerators, ranging from 50 to 99 liters, which showcase their contents—commonly found in conference rooms, reception areas, and kiosks. Their dimensions are similar to those of sealed models of the same capacity.

Among the 85 models, there are also two double-door models, each with a capacity of 80 liters and widths of 43 and 52.5 cm. According to the spec sheet, in one of them, 26 of the 80 liters are dedicated to the freezer compartment. There are also retro-style models, in black and cream, with roughly the same dimensions.

sections.heading: What to Measure Before Ordering
paragraphs: The clearance height under a table or countertop, plus ventilation space. Width—all models measured are narrower than 53 cm, but if placing next to a table or cabinet, make sure the door opens fully. Depth—41 to 53.5 cm, so they all fit within the depth of a standard table. And a power outlet must be available, without having to share a power strip with computers.

faq.question: How tall is an office refrigerator?
faq.answer: Our catalog lists two height ranges: 44 to 51 cm for 50-liter mini-bar models, and 82.5 to 85 cm for models ranging from 80 to 99 liters.

faq.question: Which office refrigerator fits under a desk?
faq.answer: Mini-bar models range in height from 44 to 51 cm. A standard office desk is usually 72 to 75 cm high, and the 85 models are taller than that.

faq.question: How wide is an office refrigerator?
faq.answer: 43 to 52.5 cm across all 16 models measured, with a depth of 41 to 53.5 cm.

faq.question: Can an office refrigerator be placed inside a closed cabinet?
faq.answer: Only if the manufacturer permits it and within the limits it specifies. An office refrigerator is designed for freestanding use and dissipates heat from the back and sides; it will have to work harder if placed in a closed cabinet.

freezer-dimensions.title: Freezer sizes—upright or chest—and what that means for the space you’ll need
freezer-dimensions.description: The upright freezers in our catalog range from 54 to 70 cm in width; chest freezers range from 94 to 139 cm in width, but are only 84 to 88 cm tall. Dimensions are listed by model, capacities, and what to measure before ordering.

sections.heading: The short answer: two types, two forms
paragraphs: 16 freezers are listed in our catalog. 11 are upright freezers: 54 to 70 cm wide, 83.5 to 191.2 cm tall, and 54 to 76.8 cm deep. Five are chest freezers: 94 to 138.6 cm wide, 84.4 to 88 cm tall, and 56 to 80 cm deep.

For a similar capacity, the difference is dramatic. The largest upright freezer in the catalog, with a capacity of 404 liters, is 70 cm wide. A 400-liter chest freezer is 138.6 cm wide—almost twice as wide. What the chest freezer gains is height: it is lower than a typical countertop.

sections.heading: Upright Freezer: By Number of Drawers
paragraphs: Three models ranging from 83.5 to 84 cm in height, 54 to 55.1 cm in width, and 75 to 97 liters in capacity—counter-height freezers. Six-drawer freezers: 54 to 55 cm wide, 143 to 169 cm tall, 174 to 194 liters. And the taller models, with seven to eight drawers: 59.5 to 70 cm wide, 185 to 191.2 cm tall, 262 to 404 liters.

With a freestanding freezer, the opening space is also important: the drawers slide out forward, so there needs to be free space in front of it that is at least as deep as the freezer itself. And just like with a refrigerator, it’s a good idea to leave ventilation space above and on the sides according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

sections.heading: Chest Freezer: Consider the Lid
paragraphs: A chest-style freezer opens upward. The lid pivots on a hinge at the back, so when it is open, it extends to approximately the height of the freezer plus its depth. For a freezer that is 85 cm high and 66 cm deep, this is about 150 cm. A shelf or cabinet above a chest-style freezer will block the opening.

The measured capacities of the chest freezers range from 212 to 419 liters, and the catalog also lists 510- and 525-liter models for which no dimensions were provided. A chest freezer is suitable for a storage room, a utility balcony, or a laundry room where there is available width along a wall.

sections.heading: What to Measure at Home Before Ordering
paragraphs: For an upright freezer: the width of the niche, the height to the cabinet or ceiling, and free space in front of it for pulling out the drawers. For a chest freezer: the length of the available wall space and the clearance above it—so the lid can open fully. For both types: a nearby electrical outlet and a clear path through doors and up stairs.

If the freezer is to be placed in an enclosed space such as a storage room, also check the climate classification on the specification sheet—it specifies the range of ambient temperatures within which the freezer is designed to operate.

faq.question: What are the dimensions of a 6-drawer freezer?
faq.answer: The three models listed in our catalog measure 54 to 55 cm in width, 143 to 169 cm in height, and 55 to 59.5 cm in depth, with a capacity of 174 to 194 liters.

faq.question: What are the dimensions of a chest freezer?
faq.answer: 94 to 138.6 cm wide, 84.4 to 88 cm tall, and 56 to 80 cm deep, with a capacity of 212 to 419 liters in the models measured. When the lid is open, it reaches approximately the height of the freezer plus its depth.

faq.question: Do you have a small, tabletop-height freezer?
faq.answer: Yes. Three models in our catalog are 83.5 to 84 cm tall, 54 to 55.1 cm wide, and have a capacity of 75 to 97 liters.

faq.question: Which takes up less space—a upright or a chest freezer?
faq.answer: In terms of floor space, the upright model. The 404-liter upright freezer in the catalog is 70 cm wide, and the 400-liter chest freezer is 138.6 cm wide. The chest freezer is low, but you need space above it to open the lid.

integrated-refrigerator-dimensions.title: Dimensions of a built-in refrigerator and the niche — 54 cm wide, with a difference in height
integrated-refrigerator-dimensions.description: The built-in refrigerators in our catalog are 54 cm wide in almost all models measured, and 55 cm deep in all of them; what varies is the height, and with it, the niche dimensions. Table by model, niche dimensions from the manufacturer’s specifications, and door mounting methods.

sections.heading: The short answer: 54 × 55 cm, and a height of 177.5 or 193.5
paragraphs: Of the six built-in refrigerators listed in our catalog, all are 55 cm deep, and five of them are 54 cm wide; the sixth, with a bottom freezer, is wider—69 cm. The height is divided into two categories: four models ranging from 177.5 to 178.5 cm in height and two at 193.5 cm. The capacity ranges from 264 to 298 liters for the 54-cm models, and 389 liters for the wider model.

This is the opposite of a freestanding refrigerator, where every dimension varies from model to model. A built-in refrigerator is designed to fit a standard niche, so the question isn’t “how wide is it,” but rather “what niche height is it intended for.”

sections.heading: Niche Dimensions
paragraphs: Two models list niche dimensions in the catalog: one requires a niche 55.5–56 cm wide, 177.8–178 cm high, and 56–59 cm deep; the other requires a niche 56 cm wide and 55 cm deep, with a height of 177.8–178.5 cm. In other words, a niche 56 cm wide and approximately 178 cm high serves as the basis for the 177.5 models.

A model that is 193.5 cm tall requires a correspondingly tall niche. Anyone replacing an existing built-in refrigerator should measure the niche itself, not the old refrigerator—and the difference between 178 and 194 is the difference between a model that fits and one that doesn’t.

sections.heading: How the door is mounted: sliding hinge or door-on-door
paragraphs: The cabinet front attaches to the refrigerator door using one of two methods, and the specification sheet indicates which one. With the “Slide Hinge” method, the cabinet door is attached to the cabinet’s hinge and slides along the refrigerator door when opened. In the “Door-on-Door” method, the cabinet front is screwed directly to the refrigerator door.

The second method has a limitation you should be aware of before ordering the cabinetry: a Samsung built-in freezer in our catalog, for example, limits the cabinet door to 25 kg and a thickness of 16 to 19 mm. A front that is heavier or thicker than that requires a different solution.

sections.heading: Side-by-side integrated refrigerator and freezer
paragraphs: The catalog features a single-door built-in refrigerator without a freezer, 289 liters, and a single-door built-in freezer, 220 liters—both measuring 54 × 177.5 × 55 cm. When placed in two adjacent niches, they form a complete 509-liter pair behind uniform cabinet fronts.

There is also a wide model: a built-in refrigerator with a bottom freezer, 69 cm wide, 389 liters, 69 × 193.5 × 55 cm, with a sliding hinge. It appears in the table, but its specification sheet does not list the niche dimensions—these must be confirmed with the importer before ordering the cabinetry.

faq.question: What are the dimensions of the niche for a built-in refrigerator?
faq.answer: For 177.5 cm models in our catalog: a niche 55.5–56 cm wide, approximately 178 cm high, and 55–59 cm deep, according to the manufacturer’s specifications. For a model that is 193.5 cm tall, a correspondingly taller niche is required. Always check the specifications for the final model.

faq.question: How wide is a built-in refrigerator?
faq.answer: Five of the six models listed in our catalog are 54 cm wide, all with a depth of 55 cm. The sixth model, which has a bottom-mounted freezer, is 69 cm wide.

faq.question: Can a standard refrigerator be installed in a built-in refrigerator niche?
faq.answer: Not recommended. A freestanding refrigerator is designed to dissipate heat into an open environment, and it will have to work harder inside a closed cabinet. Furthermore, the narrowest freestanding refrigerator in our catalog is 54.9 cm wide and 56.8 cm deep, and most are even deeper.

faq.question: What is the difference between a sliding hinge and a door-on-door hinge?
faq.answer: The sliding cabinet front is hinged to the cabinet and slides along the refrigerator door. In the “door-on-door” configuration, it is screwed directly to the refrigerator door; in this case, there are weight and thickness limitations for the front panel, which are listed in the specifications sheet.

refrigerator-70cm-wide.title: 70-centimeter-wide refrigerator—dimensions vary by model, with a capacity of up to 470 liters
refrigerator-70cm-wide.description: The 70-centimeter-wide refrigerators listed in our catalog measure 70 to 70.5 centimeters in width, 170.8 to 185 centimeters in height, and 63.5 to 72 centimeters in depth. A table by model, and why almost all of them have a top-mounted freezer.

sections.heading: The short answer: 70 cm, 329 to 470 liters
paragraphs: Eleven freestanding refrigerators with widths ranging from 65 to 72 cm were listed in our catalog: ten of them are exactly 70 cm wide, and one is 70.5 cm wide. The height ranges from 170.8 to 185 cm, the depth from 63.5 to 72 cm, and the capacity from 329 to 470 liters.

This is a useful intermediate width: A 60-cm-wide refrigerator in our selection has a capacity of up to 344 liters, and ten out of the 11 models with a width of 70 cm are larger—ranging from 381 to 470 liters, meaning up to 126 additional liters. The exception is a 329-liter model, which is why we compare liters and not just width. And compared to the 80 series, which starts at 75 cm in our store, it fits into niches where a wider refrigerator would no longer fit.

sections.heading: Almost all of them have a top-mounted freezer
paragraphs: Ten of the 11 models are labeled “top-freezer,” and the eleventh is a “versatile” model from Hisense. None of the 70-wide upright refrigerators in our catalog are labeled as bottom-freezer models. Those looking for a “combination” model—a bottom-freezer refrigerator—can choose from our catalog among models ranging from 60 to 76 cm wide and larger.

The only exception is a built-in refrigerator: The catalog lists a built-in model with a bottom freezer that is 69 cm wide and has a capacity of 389 liters; its specification sheet lists the dimensions as 69 × 193.5 × 55 cm. It is designed to be built into a cabinet niche rather than freestanding, and therefore does not appear in this table.

sections.heading: Depth and Height
paragraphs: The depth ranges from 63.5 to 72 cm, so all models will protrude somewhat from cabinets that are about 60 cm deep. The three shallowest models, at 63.5 cm, are also among the shortest—172 cm.

Height is divided into two groups: 170.8 to 178.5 cm, and 182.5 to 185 cm for models ranging from 466 to 470 liters. If there is a cabinet above the niche, this difference of an additional 5 to 10 cm for ventilation can be decisive.

sections.heading: What to Measure at Home
paragraphs: Niche width: A 70-cm-wide refrigerator requires a niche wider than the unit itself, with clearance for installation and ventilation as specified by the manufacturer. The height should extend to the cabinet above. The depth should extend to the wall. And regarding door opening direction—a refrigerator with a top-mounted freezer has two doors, and both must open fully.
If you already have the dimensions of the niche, send them to us via WhatsApp and we’ll check which models we have in stock.

freestanding-range-dimensions.title: Dimensions of a combination oven and cooktop — 60 × 60 × 85, and how they vary between models
freestanding-range-dimensions.description: Freestanding combination ovens are available in widths of 50, 60, or 90 cm. Dimensions are measured by model according to the specification sheets; height is adjustable from 85 to 90 cm; oven capacity depends on width; and these details should be verified in-store before placing an order.

sections.heading: The short answer: 60 wide, 60 deep, 85 high
paragraphs: Our catalog features 16 freestanding cooktop-and-oven combinations, 15 of which list their dimensions in the specifications sheet. Eleven of them are 60 cm wide, three are 50 cm wide, and one is 90 cm wide. The depth is 60 cm for almost all of them, and the height is 85 cm—in some models, it is adjustable up to 90 cm.
The table below lists the models whose data sheets are in a format that the table can read; the information in the paragraphs covers all 15 data sheets.

sections.heading: Height: Why Are the Legs Adjustable?
paragraphs: A freestanding combination oven stands between the kitchen cabinets, and its cooktop is designed to be flush with the countertop. Eight models have a fixed height of 85 cm, and six are adjustable: four in the 85–90 cm range, one in the 85–87 cm range, and one—which is 90 cm wide—in the 85–90.5 cm range.

If your kitchen countertop is higher than 85 cm, a model with adjustable legs will allow you to level the cooktop to match the countertop height. A model with a fixed height will leave a step. Measure the countertop height from the floor before making your selection.

sections.heading: 50, 60, or 90 cm: What You Get at Each Width
paragraphs: 60 cm: Oven capacity ranging from 56 to 72 liters in the published catalogs, and most models have four burners—the most powerful of which, in catalogs that specify this, has a power output of 2.9 to 4.2 kilowatts. This is the standard, and a new combination oven of this width will almost always fit in place of an old one.

50 cm: Capacity of 46 to 54 liters, still with four burners. Suitable for a small kitchen or a student apartment. One of the narrowest and most compact models—50 cm wide and 75 cm high according to the spec sheet—so it’s lower than the countertop and won’t be flush with it. The model name specifies a depth of 55 cm, while the catalog lists 50 cm, so it does not appear in the table; we will verify its depth with the manufacturer.

90 cm: The model listed with these dimensions has an oven capacity of 94 liters and five burners, and the catalog also features a 90-cm model with six burners. Upgrading from a 60-cm oven to a 90-cm oven requires an additional 30 cm between the cabinets—meaning a change to the kitchen layout.

sections.heading: What to check in-store before placing an order
paragraphs: The width between the cabinets, and whether there is any clearance required by the manufacturer on the sides. The height of the countertop relative to the height of the oven. The gas connection: its location behind the oven and the required length of the hose—the connection must be made by a certified gas technician. Electrical outlet for the ignition and the oven. And above the cooktop: the distance to the range hood or upper cabinet is specified in the installation instructions for each model.

And don’t forget the oven door: it opens downward and forward, so you need clear space in front of it. In a narrow kitchen or in front of an island, this is the dimension that determines whether you can stand in front of an open oven.

microwave-dimensions.description: Width, height, and depth of microwaves by model, from the specification sheets in the catalog: A 20-liter microwave is about 44 cm wide, while 30-liter and larger models are 52–54 cm wide—and built-in microwaves are a different story.

paragraphs: Among the 33 freestanding microwaves listed in our catalog, the width ranges from 43.4 to 53.8 cm, the height ranges from 24.1 to 32.5 cm, and the depth ranges from 31.5 to 42.5 cm. 20 liters (12 models): 43.4 to 45.6 cm wide, 24.1 to 26.3 cm tall, 31.5 to 36 cm deep. 23 to 26 liters (18 models): 46.9 to 51.3 cm wide, 27.2 to 31 cm tall, 33.7 to 40.6 cm deep. 30 liters and above (three models): 52 to 53.8 cm wide, 30 to 32.5 cm high, 41 to 42.5 cm deep.

sections.heading: On the Countertop: Depth and Door
paragraphs: Kitchen countertops are typically about 60 cm deep, so all the microwaves measured fit in terms of depth—but a microwave with a capacity of 30 liters or more, with a depth of 41 to 42.5 cm, leaves less than 20 cm of free space in front of it. If the countertop is narrow or has outlets and a back wall, this becomes noticeable.

The door is the often-overlooked factor. In most freestanding microwaves, the door opens sideways on a hinge, so a microwave squeezed into a corner needs space for the door to open. In addition, manufacturers require ventilation space above and behind the microwave—the exact requirements are listed in the installation instructions for each model, and a microwave that is blocked may overheat.

sections.heading: Built-in microwave: 60 cm wide, with variable depth
paragraphs: Three built-in microwaves were listed in our catalog, ranging from 25 to 34 liters. All are 59.2 to 59.5 cm wide and 38.8 to 39 cm tall—the front is designed to fit a 60-cm-wide cabinet. However, the depth ranges from 36.8 to 46.8 cm, a difference of 10 cm.

A 45 cm-high niche is a different story: That’s the height of a compact oven, and in our catalog, we have combination microwave ovens at that height, 59.5 cm wide and 45.5 to 45.6 cm high. Two product sheets list niche dimensions: one is 56 cm wide, 45 cm high, and 55 cm deep; the other is 56 cm wide, 44.6 cm high, and 54.9 cm deep.

sections.heading: What to Measure at Home

For built-in microwaves: the width, height, and depth of the niche itself, compared to the niche dimensions listed in the specifications—not the microwave’s dimensions.
