water-heater-how-long.title: How Long to Run a Water Heater in Winter and Summer — Table by Capacity
water-heater-how-long.description: How long does it take to heat a 60- to 200-liter water heater in winter, spring, and summer; how much does it cost at the 2026 rate; and how long does the hot water last for two or three showers—with a table and a calculator.

sections.heading: You don't need to heat the entire water heater
paragraphs: A shower consists of water at about 40 degrees Celsius—hot water from the water heater mixed with cold water. A 40-liter shower in winter uses only about 25 liters of 55-degree water from the water heater. Three showers total about 75 liters, half of a 150-liter hot water urn. The hot water rises to the top of the hot water urn and is drawn from there, so partial heating works.

In practice: A 150-liter water heater provides enough hot water for three showers in the winter in about an hour and a half, at a cost of about 2.33 NIS. Heating the water for a full three hours costs twice as much and provides hot water, most of which will cool down in the water heater by tomorrow.

sections.heading: How to Calculate
paragraphs: Heating one liter of water by one degree requires 4.186 kilojoules. 150 liters from 15 to 55 degrees: 150 × 4.186 × 40 ÷ 3,600 = approximately 7 kWh, plus about 5% heat loss. A 2.5-kilowatt heating element delivers 2.5 kWh per hour, so it takes about three hours to fully heat the water. One hour of operation costs about 1.59 NIS.

sections.heading: Solar water heater and timer
paragraphs: In most homes in the north, the solar water heater is sufficient from April through October, and on sunny winter days it provides partial heating—so the actual operating time is shorter than shown in the table. A timer (a Shabbat timer for the water heater) that turns on the water heater about an hour and a half before shower time saves most of the energy lost when the water heater is left on all day.

faq.question: How long should you let the water heater run for one shower?
faq.answer: In winter, with a 150-liter water heater with a 2.5-kilowatt heating element: about 30–35 minutes for a 40-liter shower. With a small 60–80-liter water heater—about 30 minutes.

faq.question: How much does it cost to run a water heater for an hour?
faq.answer: A 2.5-kilowatt heating element consumes 2.5 kWh per hour—about 1.59 NIS at a rate of 63.52 agorot per kWh. A 3-kilowatt heating element — about 1.91 NIS.

faq.question: Should I leave the water heater on all the time?
faq.answer: No. A water heater that stays on all day keeps the water hot even when no one needs it and constantly wastes heat. Turning it on with a timer before showers is cheaper.

refrigerator-electricity-consumption.title: How much electricity does a refrigerator use, and how much does it cost per month?
refrigerator-electricity-consumption.description: How many kWh does a refrigerator use per year? How much does that cost per month at 2026 rates? How do you read the energy label, and when does replacing an old refrigerator pay for itself? Includes a table and a calculator.

sections.heading: The refrigerator is the biggest energy consumer in the home
paragraphs: A refrigerator runs 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Even if its power consumption is low—100–200 watts—it adds up to a significant portion of the bill: about 4% of an average household’s energy consumption for a new refrigerator, and twice that for an old one.

We reviewed our catalog in October 2026: Most of the refrigerators for which the manufacturer has published annual energy consumption figures range from 230 to 370 kWh per year, including large 4-door models. The most energy-efficient refrigerator we currently carry—as well as the energy consumption of each model—can be viewed in the refrigerator calculator.

sections.heading: Why don't we multiply watts by 24?
paragraphs: A common misconception: A 150-watt refrigerator × 24 hours = 3.6 kWh per day, more than 1,300 per year. That’s four times the actual amount. The compressor operates intermittently—the refrigerator, freezer, and air conditioner are controlled by a thermostat—and in an inverter refrigerator, it operates at low power most of the time.

The correct figure is the annual consumption listed on the energy label (kWh/year), measured under standardized conditions. Multiply it by the rate to get the annual cost: 300 kWh × 0.6352 ₪ = 190.56 ₪.

sections.heading: When does replacing an item pay for itself?
paragraphs: A refrigerator that is 15 years old or older often consumes 500–800 kWh per year, especially if the rubber seals are worn out and the condenser is dusty. Replacing a refrigerator that consumes 600 kWh with a 255 kWh model saves 345 kWh per year—about 219 NIS per year and about 2,600 NIS over the refrigerator’s 12-year lifespan.

It won’t pay for a new refrigerator on its own, but it covers a significant portion of the cost—and when your old refrigerator starts acting up, that’s what makes the decision easy. The most reliable way to figure out how much your old refrigerator consumes: measure the power usage per week, then multiply by 52.

sections.heading: How to reduce the energy consumption of your current refrigerator
paragraphs: Leave a 5–10 cm gap behind and above the condenser vents, and keep it away from the stove and direct sunlight. Dust the condenser once a year. Set the temperature to 4 degrees in the refrigerator compartment and minus 18 in the freezer—colder temperatures don’t preserve food better; they just cost more. And check the door gaskets: if a sheet of paper can be tucked under the door and pulled out easily, the seal isn’t tight enough.

faq.question: How many kWh does a refrigerator consume per day?
faq.answer: New family-sized refrigerator: 0.6–1 kWh per day (230–370 per year). Old, large refrigerator: 1.5–2 kWh per day or more.

faq.question: Do 4-door refrigerators use more electricity?
faq.answer: They generally use slightly more energy than a standard refrigerator of the same quality because they’re larger—but less than you might think. In our catalog, large 4-door refrigerators usually consume around 300–360 kWh per year—not far off from smaller standard refrigerators, and certainly less than an old refrigerator.

faq.question: Does Shabbat mode increase energy consumption?
faq.answer: Minimal. In Saturday mode, the lighting and sensors are deactivated, and the compressor operates on a fixed schedule; the impact on the annual bill is negligible.

air-conditioner-running-cost.title: How much does it cost to run an air conditioner? Calculation based on horsepower and hours
air-conditioner-running-cost.description: How much does an hour of air conditioning cost, a whole night, and a month in the summer?—A table based on air conditioner size using 2026 electricity rates, the difference between inverter and ON/OFF models, and how to lower your bill.

sections.heading: How to calculate how much electricity an air conditioner uses
paragraphs: An air conditioner does not consume its BTU rating. The BTU rating represents the amount of cooling it produces, and the electricity it consumes is less than that amount by a factor equal to the coefficient of performance (COP). A 12,000 BTU air conditioner produces about 3.5 kilowatts of cooling; with a COP of 3.5, it consumes about 1 kilowatt of electricity. Multiply that by 63.52 agorot—about 64 agorot per hour at full capacity.

An inverter air conditioner does not operate at full capacity most of the time. Once the room reaches the set temperature, it reduces its output and maintains that temperature; therefore, under normal use, the average load is 50%–70%. The table is based on 70%—a scenario typical of a hot day.

sections.heading: Inverter vs. ON/OFF
paragraphs: An ON/OFF air conditioner operates at full power until the room reaches the set temperature, then turns off and turns back on when the temperature rises. Each time it starts up, the compressor draws a high current, and the room temperature spikes. On an exceptionally hot day, the difference in energy consumption is small; over the course of an entire season, and especially at night, an inverter unit typically saves tens of percent.

There’s another side to this: The energy efficiency ratings of new inverter air conditioners (SEER, SCOP) are much higher than those of a 15-year-old air conditioner. An old air conditioner operating at a COP of 2.5 consumes about 40% more energy than a new air conditioner with a COP of 3.5 to provide the same cooling.

sections.heading: Heating in Winter
paragraphs: An air conditioner is one of the most cost-effective ways to heat a home: with a COP of 3.5 or higher, it produces three times as much heat as the electricity it consumes, whereas a space heater or oil-filled radiator produces exactly the amount of electricity it consumes. A 2,000-watt radiator costs about 1.27 NIS per hour; a 1.25-horsepower air conditioner that heats the same room costs about 40–60 agorot.

sections.heading: How to pay the bill
paragraphs: 24–25 degrees in the summer instead of 20: Every degree saves a few percent on energy consumption. Close the blinds on the sunny side during the afternoon. Clean the filters once a month during the season—a clogged filter reduces efficiency and increases energy consumption. And for inverter air conditioners: don’t turn them off and on every hour, because restarting is the most energy-intensive part of operation.

faq.question: How much does it cost to run an air conditioner all night?
faq.answer: A 1-c.s. air conditioner, running for 8 hours at an average load of 70%: about 2.68 NIS per night, about 80.42 NIS per month. 1.5-k"s air conditioner: about 4.02 NIS per night.

faq.question: Which costs more—an air conditioner or a space heater?
faq.answer: Heater. A 2,000-watt radiator or space heater consumes 2 kWh per hour—about 1.27 NIS. An inverter air conditioner heats the same room for one-third to one-half of that amount, because it transfers heat from outside rather than generating it.

faq.question: Where can I find the energy efficiency rating for the air conditioner?
faq.answer: In the specifications, as COP or EER (instantaneous cooling) or SEER/SCOP (seasonal average). For most air conditioners in our catalog, this information appears on the product page.

air-conditioner-size-for-room.title: How many horsepower does an air conditioner need for a room? Table by square meter
air-conditioner-size-for-room.description: How to choose an air conditioner size based on room area and number of people, a table of horsepower and BTU ratings for each room size, and when to go one size up—with a calculator and models from the catalog.

sections.heading: The first question when buying an air conditioner
paragraphs: Before considering the brand, energy rating, or price, you need to know what size air conditioner you need. An air conditioner that’s too small runs at full capacity all the time, fails to reach the desired temperature on a hot day in the north, and consumes more electricity. An air conditioner that’s too large cools quickly and then shuts off, removes less humidity, and leaves the room cold and sticky—and costs more to buy.

In Israel, air conditioner size is measured in horsepower (hp), but the number that really matters is the cooling capacity in BTU. The standard conversion in the market is 1 hp ≈ 9,000 BTU. This is a convention rather than a standard, which is why each air conditioner page in our catalog also lists the BTU rating published by the manufacturer.

sections.heading: The formula: 650 BTU per square meter plus 500 per person
paragraphs: The rule of thumb published by manufacturers in Israel is 650 BTU per square meter of room space, plus 500 BTU for each person who is usually in the room. A 16-square-meter room with two people: 16 × 650 + 2 × 500 = 11,400 BTU, which is approximately 1.27 HP—a 1.25 HP air conditioner, or 1.5 HP if the room is particularly hot.
The table below converts these measurements to common sizes and rounds them to the nearest size sold on the market.

sections.heading: When to go up one size
paragraphs: An upper floor under the roof or a tiled roof, large windows facing south or west, an open-concept living room and kitchen, a ceiling higher than 2.7 meters, or a room with a gaming computer or heat-generating equipment. In any of these cases, it’s a good idea to go up a size—from 1.5 to 2 c.s., for example.
For a large living room with a non-standard layout, it’s best not to rely on the chart. Send us the room’s dimensions, orientation, and floor via WhatsApp, and we’ll recommend a size and model.

sections.heading: The right size means lower electricity bills
paragraphs: A properly sized inverter air conditioner operates most of the time at about 50%–70% of its capacity. An air conditioner that is too small is forced to operate at 100% capacity, so it is not only less comfortable—it is also more expensive to run than a unit one size larger. You can check the cost based on size in the guide “How Much Does It Cost to Run an Air Conditioner?” or directly using the calculator.

faq.question: How many horsepower should an air conditioner be for a bedroom?
faq.answer: A 9–12 m² bedroom occupied by one or two people requires 7,000–8,800 BTU—a 1-c.s. air conditioner. A large 15–18 m² bedroom requires 1.25–1.5 c.s.

faq.question: How many horsepower for a 30-square-meter living room?
faq.answer: 30 square meters with four people: 30 × 650 + 4 × 500 = 21,500 BTU, about 2.4 horsepower—a 2.5-horsepower air conditioner. An open-concept living room connected to the kitchen or on an upper floor requires 3 c.s.

faq.question: How many BTUs is 1 hp?
faq.answer: According to industry standards in the Israeli market, approximately 9,000 BTU. In practice, 1-horsepower air conditioners range from 8,500 to 9,800 BTU, so it’s a good idea to check the BTU rating in the specifications.

appliance-electricity-consumption-table.title: Table of Electricity Consumption for Household Appliances (2026)
appliance-electricity-consumption-table.description: How much electricity does each appliance in the home consume, and what is the cost per hour and per month: refrigerator, washing machine, tumble dryer, dishwasher, oven, cooktop, Shabbat hotplate, space heater, and more—based on the 2026 electricity rates.

sections.heading: How to Read the Table
paragraphs: The power ratings and times in the table are typical estimates, not measurements for a specific model. Actual consumption depends on the model, the cycle, and usage habits—a washing machine on a 90-degree cycle consumes several times more than on a 30-degree “Eco” cycle. To calculate consumption for your specific appliance, enter the power rating from the label into the calculator.
The formula is simple: power in watts ÷ 1,000 × hours = kWh, and each kWh costs 63.52 agorot, including VAT. A 2,000-watt appliance running for half an hour consumes one kWh.

sections.heading: What Really Makes a Difference in the Bill
paragraphs: What matters is not the power rating, but the power rating multiplied by the time. A 2,000-watt kettle that runs for 12 minutes a day costs less per month than a 50-watt fan that runs all night in the summer and a TV that’s on for four hours. On the other hand, a 3,000-watt tumble dryer that runs for an hour and a half every day is one of the biggest energy consumers in the home.

In winter, space heaters and radiators are usually the reason for a spike in the utility bill: 2,000 watts, three hours a day, costs about 115 NIS a month per room. An inverter air conditioner heats the same room for one-third to one-half of that cost.

sections.heading: Where a New Product Saves You Money
paragraphs: For appliances that run for many hours: refrigerators (year-round), air conditioners (seasonal), and tumble dryers for those who dry clothes every day—a heat pump tumble dryer uses about half as much energy as a condenser tumble dryer. For appliances that run for just a few minutes a day—such as a kettle, microwave, or coffee maker—an energy-efficient model will make almost no difference to your bill, so it’s best to choose them based on convenience and quality.

sections.heading: Shabbat hotplate and hot water urn
paragraphs: A 400-watt Shabbat hotplate that stays on for 24 hours consumes about 9.6 kWh—about 6 NIS per Shabbat and about 24 NIS per month. A 2,000-watt hot water urn consumes a lot of energy during the initial heating phase and then only maintains the temperature. During holidays lasting two or three days, the cost accumulates accordingly.

faq.question: How much does it cost to run a washing machine?
faq.answer: A standard cycle on a new machine consumes 0.5–1 kWh—32 to 64 agorot. A hot cycle at 60–90 degrees consumes 1.5–2 kWh. Most of the energy goes toward heating the water, not the motor.

faq.question: How much does it cost to run an oven?
faq.answer: A 2,000–3,000-watt oven that bakes for one hour consumes 1.5–2.5 kWh (the thermostat turns the heating elements on and off)—about 1 to 1.60 NIS per baking session.

faq.question: Does being on hold cost money?
faq.answer: Just a little. A device that consumes 5 watts while on standby 24 hours a day uses about 44 kWh per year—about 28 NIS. When you add up several such devices, the impact becomes noticeable.

electricity-price-per-kwh-2026.title: 2026 Electricity Rates: How Much Does a kWh Cost, and What Does That Mean for Your Home Appliances?
electricity-price-per-kwh-2026.description: Residential electricity rate for 2026 — 63.52 agorot per kWh, including VAT, effective July 1, 2026. How much does it cost to run an appliance for an hour, how does the energy efficiency rating translate to shekels, and what about private providers?

sections.heading: What is a kWh?
paragraphs: A kilowatt-hour (kWh) is the unit used to measure electricity consumption: a 1,000-watt appliance running for one hour consumes one kWh. A 100-watt appliance takes ten hours to consume the same kWh. Each kWh is billed according to the rate—and the bill also includes a fixed charge and a capacity charge that are independent of consumption.

sections.heading: How prices are set and when they change
paragraphs: The Electricity Authority updates the residential rate twice a year—on January 1 and July 1. As of July 1, 2026, the rate is 53.83 agorot per kWh before VAT (in January 2026: 54.51). The rate consists of a generation component, a system component, and a grid component, to which VAT (18%) is added.
The calculators on this site and on the “Kama Yotze” site use the same rates and are updated simultaneously, so the results on both sites are identical.

sections.heading: Private suppliers
paragraphs: Since the electricity market was liberalized, consumers can switch to a private electricity provider that offers a discount on the consumption component—usually a fixed 5%–7%, or 15%–20% on nighttime plans or during certain hours. In the calculators, you can enter the rate after the discount. A nighttime plan is especially worthwhile for those who run heavy-duty appliances—dishwashers, washing machines, and tumble dryers—during those hours.

sections.heading: What does it mean when you choose an appliance?
paragraphs: Every 100 kWh per year difference between two models is worth about 64 NIS per year. For a refrigerator that operates for 12–15 years, a difference of 100 kWh adds up to about 760–950 NIS—an amount that might justify choosing a slightly more expensive model. For an appliance that runs for only a few minutes a day, such as a kettle, that same difference in energy rating makes almost no difference.

Therefore, our recommendation is to compare the annual energy consumption in kWh—not just the energy efficiency rating—and to factor in how many hours the appliance actually runs. For products in this catalog, the consumption figure appears in the specifications as published by the manufacturer; if not, send us the model name and we’ll check.

faq.question: How much will a kilowatt-hour of electricity cost in 2026?
faq.answer: As of July 1, 2026: 53.83 agorot before VAT, 63.52 agorot including VAT. From January through June 2026, the price was 54.51 agorot before VAT.

faq.question: When are electricity rates updated?
faq.answer: Twice a year, on January 1 and July 1, as determined by the Electricity Authority. Next update: January 1, 2027.

faq.question: How much does it cost to run an air conditioner for an hour?
faq.answer: A 1-c.s. air conditioner with an energy efficiency ratio of 3.5 consumes about 0.75 kilowatts at full power—about 48 agorot per hour. A 2-c.s. air conditioner—about 96 agorot.
